one_line_description.value: Copper is a CRM that helps teams be there for their clients at every stage of the customer journey.
one_line_description.quote: The CRM that helps you be there for your clients, every step of the way.

has_public_api.quote: The Copper Developer API ("Dev API") provides a RESTful interface with JSON-formatted responses to access most Copper resources.

api_type.quote: provides a RESTful interface with JSON-formatted responses

api_breadth.value: REST/JSON, broad read-write coverage of most Copper resources (leads, people, companies, opportunities, projects, tasks, activities) plus webhooks for create/update/delete

docs_url.quote: The Copper Web API allows you to access and build your own applications that interact with Copper in more complex ways than the integrations we provide out of the box.

auth_methods.quote: There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0.

access_model.quote: To generate an API token, in the Copper web app go to System settings > API Keys and click the 'GENERATE API KEY' button.

access_notes.value: Any admin user in a Copper workspace can generate an API key self-serve from System settings > API Keys; no vendor approval, app review, or partner program is documented for API keys. OAuth2.0 is the preferred authentication approach for partner integrations. A Copper workspace/plan is still required, and the vendor-hosted MCP server is a separate early-access beta (launches November 2026) with no published endpoint.
access_notes.quote: Admins can see all user generated tokens and generate new ones.

official_mcp_server.quote: Yes. Copper is launching an official MCP server, built and hosted by Copper. The beta launches in November 2026.

rate_limits.value: 180 requests per minute per account (429 on exceed, rolling window); bulk APIs additionally limited to 3 requests per second; webhook notifications 600 per minute per account and 1,800 per 10 minutes, max 100 active subscriptions
rate_limits.quote: All API calls are limited to 180 requests per minute. Once this limit has been reached, calls will return an error response with status code `429`.

webhooks.quote: Webhooks allow systems integrated with Copper to receive near real-time notification of certain events so that data updates and workflows can be triggered.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Undocumented endpoints may change without notice; incompatible changes (removing versions/endpoints, new required params, removed fields) are deprecated with advance notice and supported for at least six months after announcement, with breaking changes announced alongside a migration plan and timeline; the API domain moved from api.prosperworks.com to api.copper.com/developer_api with auto-redirects until early 2022.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: We will continue to support deprecated APIs for at least six months from the announcement to allow partners to transition their integrations.

verdict_reason: Copper exposes a public REST/JSON Developer API covering most resources, with self-serve API key generation for admin users plus OAuth2.0 for partner integrations. Documented rate limits (180 req/min), webhooks, Postman resources, and a 65-tool Composio toolkit make it straightforward to build against. No app review, partner approval, or sales contact is documented as a gate for API keys, though access presumes a Copper workspace/plan.
open_questions: Whether API access requires a specific paid Copper plan tier: the plans feature-comparison support page was only available as a search snippet, not full text, and the pricing page text fetched does not state an API gating rule.
OAuth2.0 scope/permission documentation was not captured in the fetched text (developer.copper.com OAuth flow/quickstart pages appeared only as snippets), so scope documentation is unconfirmed.
No documented sandbox/test environment was found; it is unclear whether developers must test against a production Copper account.

Only the embedded 'Copper App SDK' (JavaScript, copper-sdk) is evidenced; it is unclear whether Copper publishes official server-side SDKs for other languages (the SDK docs describe an in-app context SDK, not a full Dev API client).
The official Copper MCP server is in beta (November 2026) and only accessible via an early-access/waitlist form; no MCP endpoint URL is published.
The Composio toolkit lists only API_KEY as its auth scheme, while Copper docs list both API keys and OAuth2.0.
No community MCP server URLs were retrieved (GitHub and MCP registry sections were empty), although Copper's MCP page references unspecified third-party connectors.
